By performing iterative local optimization constrained to this manifold, RNAGenScape preserves favorable computational viability proxies, accesses reliable guidance, and discourages excursions into regions poorly supported by the training data. The framework integrates three components: (1) an autoencoder jointly trained with a property predictor to learn a property-organized latent manifold, (2) a denoising autoencoder that projects updates back onto the manifold, and (3) a property-guided Langevin dynamics procedure that performs optimization along the manifold. Across three real-world mRNA datasets spanning two orders of magnitude in size, RNAGenScape increases median oracle-predicted property gain by up to 267% and success rate by up to 31%, while maintaining good biological viability proxy measures and achieving competitive inference efficiency compared to existing generative approaches.

Machine Learning.title: Text-Aware, Vision-Blind: How Multimodal Image Editing Systems Handle Unsafe Inputs
Machine Learning.summary: Multimodal image generation systems have made rapid progress and increasingly emphasize content safety. However, their safety mechanisms tend to rely on a single modality and lack joint consideration of both visual content and text prompts, particularly in instruction-guided image editing, where the uploaded image may itself carry risk. We thus introduce EditSafetyBench, a benchmark that measures system-level safety awareness of advanced image editing systems, containing 5,940 image-instruction pairs, covering safe and unsafe images across 11 risk categories and three edit intents. We then probe the benchmark dataset on four systems, including Gemini, GPT, Qwen API, and Qwen Local. Based on our evaluation, we observe a systematic text-vision safety mismatch: Gemini and GPT refuse 87.1\% and 81.6\% cases containing unsafe-intent editing prompts, while only refusing 24.2\% and 22.4\% cases with both unsafe images and neutral instructions. At the category level, most risks are considered inconsistently by different systems, e.g., GPT allows 70.4\% editing attempts of unsafe political content while Gemini only allows 34.8\%. Notably, sexual content shows the strongest visual sensitivity, likely benefiting from mature NSFW identification works. Our findings highlight the need for safety guardrails that jointly reason over both visual and textual modalities in image editing systems.

Machine Learning.title: Beyond Visual Fidelity: Benchmarking Super-Resolution Models for Large-Scale Remote Sensing Imagery via Downstream Task Integration
Machine Learning.summary: Super-resolution (SR) techniques have made major advances in reconstructing high-resolution images from low-resolution inputs. The increased resolution provides visual enhancement and utility for monitoring tasks. In particular, SR has been increasingly developed for satellite-based Earth observation, with applications in urban planning, agriculture, ecology, and disaster response. However, existing SR studies and benchmarks typically use fidelity metrics such as PSNR or SSIM, whereas the true utility of super-resolved images lies in supporting downstream tasks such as land cover classification, biomass estimation, and change detection. To bridge this gap, we introduce GeoSR-Bench, a downstream task-integrated SR benchmark dataset to evaluate SR models beyond fidelity metrics. GeoSR-Bench comprises spatially co-located, temporally aligned, and quality-controlled image pairs from about 36,000 locations across diverse land covers, spanning resolutions from 500m to 0.6m. To the best of our knowledge, GeoSR-Bench is the first SR benchmark that directly connects improved image resolution from SR models with downstream Earth monitoring tasks, including land cover segmentation, infrastructure mapping, and biophysical variable estimation. Using GeoSR-Bench, we benchmark GAN, transformer, neural operator, and diffusion-based SR models on perceptual quality and downstream task performance. We conduct experiments with 270 settings, covering 2 cross-platform SR tasks, 9 SR models, 3 downstream task models, and 5 downstream tasks for each SR task. The results show that improvements in traditional SR metrics often do not correlate with gains in task performance, and the correlations can be negative, indicating that these metrics provide limited guidance for selecting superior models for downstream tasks. This reveals the need to integrate downstream tasks into SR model development and evaluation.
Machine Learning.comment: Under review at Remote Sensing of Environment (RSE)

Machine Learning.title: Automating the Expert Eye: A System-Agnostic Deep Learning Framework for Rare Event Discovery in Imbalanced Force Spectroscopy
Machine Learning.summary: Single-molecule force spectroscopy (SMFS) probes biomolecular mechanics at the single-molecule level, but high-throughput acquisition of force-extension curves creates a data processing bottleneck. Identifying rare specific unbinding events among thousands of noise-dominated traces still relies largely on manual visual inspection. Here, we present a deep learning workflow for the preliminary screening of severely imbalanced SMFS datasets. Using 2D image representations of force-extension curves without system-specific physical priors, we fine-tuned a modified ResNet18 architecture trained with focal loss and evaluated it on the mechanical unfolding pathways of the Ruminococcus champanellensis XMod-Doc/Coh complex. On a held-out test set with a 1.34% target prevalence (13 positive P_2 events among 970 curves), the model achieved 92.31% recall (12 of 13 events) and 91.95% specificity (880 of 957 negative traces), automatically discarding 90.82% of the dataset and reducing manual review from 970 to 89 flagged curves. We also integrated Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) to provide a qualitative visual reference of the curve regions driving each prediction. The complete Python pipeline is released as open-source software with an executable Google Colab notebook, enabling reproducible SMFS screening without dedicated local GPU hardware.
Machine Learning.comment: v2: Clarified methods and threshold calibration, updated test-set reporting, and refined text. 11 pages, 3 figures, 2 tables

Machine Learning.title: Channel-Dependent State Space Model for Multivariate Time Series Forecasting
Machine Learning.summary: Multivariate time series forecasting (MTSF) is critical across many real-world domains. Existing deep learning approaches fall into two paradigms with distinct limitations: channel-independent (CI) methods ignore cross-variable dependencies and model only temporal dynamics, while channel-dependent (CD) methods consider both but typically rely on architectural compromises to mitigate overfitting and computational overhead. We therefore propose Chameleon, a CD state space model (SSM) that enables data-dependent, fine-grained interactions across variables while scaling linearly with the number of variables. By connecting selective SSMs with the Kalman filter, we adapt the latter's measurement-update formulation for cross-variable modeling while preserving the SSM backbone for robust temporal modeling. We further identify favorable inductive biases of GatedDeltaNet for time series, adapt it as our backbone, and improve generalization through additional techniques, including a previously unexplored stochastic perturbation of reversible instance normalization. On strongly dependent ODE and PEMS datasets, Chameleon achieves the best MSE and MAE across all settings, while its CI ablation and prior CD methods incur 61-178% higher MSE on average. Across 28 standard benchmark settings, Chameleon also achieves better MSE and MAE than each baseline in at least 27 and 22 cases, respectively. Training-time, FLOP, and peak-memory analyses on Traffic and ETT further demonstrate competitive efficiency and favorable scalability across different variable counts.

Machine Learning.title: PhoneWorld: From Real-App Trajectories to Dynamic and Verifiable Environments for Phone-Use Agents
Machine Learning.summary: Real applications provide the training setting closest to phone-agent deployment, but are difficult to reset, scale safely, and verify programmatically. Static screenshots and interaction trajectories preserve realistic evidence but cannot generate new experience. We introduce PhoneWorld, a trace-grounded framework that converts such evidence into runnable, resettable, and verifiable Android environments. PhoneWorld induces a usage-weighted interaction skeleton from observed pages, transitions, and state-changing operations; translates it into a behavior-grounded app specification; realizes the specification through an autonomous build--inspect--repair loop; and synthesizes executable tasks with programmatic verifiers. The resulting suite spans 34 consumer-facing apps across 16 domains and supports an audited online benchmark, verified trajectory generation, and online RL through common reset and verification interfaces. Evaluations with diverse general and open-source GUI agents show that PhoneWorld supports reliable end-to-end online interaction and exposes capabilities complementary to AndroidWorld. Controlled SFT experiments further show that PhoneWorld trajectories complement AndroidWorld supervision, transfer across online and offline benchmarks, and become more effective as data volume and app coverage increase. Under a matched RL budget, combining PhoneWorld mock-app rollouts with real-app rollouts improves performance over real-app RL alone on both real-phone tasks and AndroidWorld. Together, these results demonstrate that trace-grounded executable abstraction can bridge realistic mobile behavior and scalable agent learning, turning limited real-app evidence into a growing supply of controllable and verifiable environments for training and evaluation.

Machine Learning.title: Cost-Aware Agentic Feature Optimization System for Fleet-Scale Ranking Models
Machine Learning.summary: Large Web platforms operate large fleets of ranking models, each selecting features from a shared pool of tens of thousands. We present an end-to-end agentic system that optimizes features across the fleet under resource constraints shared across models and those set per model, such as feature pipeline cost and serving throughput (QPS), respectively. In this system, LLM agents propose hypotheses, and deterministic tools execute experiments and verify them. For each model, an LLM generates and shortlists cross features from a combinatorial candidate space, and all features are then ranked by several importance methods. Feature blending mixes these rankings into a single selection, using Pareto fronts across tasks for multi-task models. An LLM Researcher agent then tunes the feature selection in 10--25 asynchronous trials under resource caps, and a trimming step keeps the pipeline cost within budget. Across production models, the system improves normalized entropy by 0.31% on average within each model's budget, and the trimming step cuts pipeline cost by 2.3% with no regression beyond measurement noise. The optimized models were launched, and in online A/B tests they improved a primary online metric by 0.20%.

Machine Learning.title: Almost Sure Convergence Rates and Concentration of Stochastic Approximation and Reinforcement Learning with Markovian Noise
Machine Learning.summary: This paper establishes, to our knowledge, the first almost sure convergence rate and the first maximal concentration bound with sub-Weibull tails for general contractive stochastic approximation algorithms with Markovian noise. As a corollary, we also obtain convergence rates in $L^p$. Key to our successes is a novel discretization of the mean ODE of stochastic approximation algorithms using intervals with diminishing (instead of constant) length. Applications yield the first almost sure convergence rate for $Q$-learning without count-based learning rates and the first maximal concentration bound for off-policy temporal difference learning, both with Markovian samples.

Machine Learning.title: GroundingPI: A Grounding Foundation Model towards Physical Intelligence with Visual Primitives
Machine Learning.summary: Precise grounding matters. It specifies which object is the target and where that object is, even in clutter and for tiny objects, and it has to be fast enough for closed-loop control. Yet vision-language-action (VLA) and world-action models (WAMs) take perception from general-purpose vision-language and video-generation backbones, which still fail in these settings. We introduce GroundingPI, a 4B grounding foundation model that generates points and boxes as quantized coordinates in a shared vocabulary. Training combines multimodal and spatial pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning with GRPO, using supervision from public datasets and dedicated data engines. Against 44 baselines across 34 grounding benchmarks spanning 11 perceptual capabilities, GroundingPI establishes a new state of the art, averaging 73.68%, above the larger GPT-6 Astra (71.54%). As a downstream visual backbone, GroundingPI improves performance on robotic manipulation and autonomous driving. Across RoboTwin 2.0 and RoboCasa-GR1, it outperforms all evaluated backbones in all four out-of-distribution settings, with relative gains of up to 24.8% over the strongest baseline. On RoboCasa-GR1, GroundingPI trained with 50% of the demonstrations outperforms those baselines trained with 75%. Its mean open-loop L2 error on nuScenes is 0.296 m. We systematically analyze GroundingPI's pretraining in scale and data composition. Grounding quality and downstream manipulation improve with pretraining scale, with generalization tracking perceptual gains most closely. Analyzing the data recipe across these 11 perceptual capabilities shows dense grounding's substantial benefits for both, and OCR's potential as a catalyst for perceptual learning. These results support grounding as a perceptual foundation, and dedicated perceptual pretraining as a promising direction for foundation models of physical intelligence.
Machine Learning.comment: 64 pages, including supplementary material. Project page: https://groundingpi.github.io/ Code: https://github.com/groundingpi/GroundingPI Model: https://huggingface.co/GroundingPI/GroundingPI

Machine Learning.title: Deterministic Temporal Embedding for Calcium Imaging Trace Extraction
Machine Learning.summary: Reliable extraction of calcium-dependent fluorescence traces in calcium imaging sequences requires identifying pixels whose fluorescence intensity reflects the same underlying cellular activity. We present a deterministic temporal embedding framework that maps pixel-wise fluorescence traces to a low-dimensional representation in which temporally coherent sources form spatially coherent regions. Starting from a fuzzy-neighborhood graph and spectral initialization, we optimize a class-balanced cross-entropy objective using exact sparse attraction and a deterministic particle-mesh decomposition of the dense repulsive interaction with sparse edge compensation, avoiding stochastic negative sampling. The resulting latent representation is spatially decoded into reliable source supports for trace extraction without imposing an explicit cellular shape prior. Experiments on synthetic and in vivo two-photon calcium imaging data demonstrate robust recovery of irregular and spatially touching sources together with efficient deterministic embedding optimization.

Machine Learning.title: The Window Lever: Longer Observation Windows Outweigh the Observed Effects of Data, Capacity, and Architecture in Customer Behavior Forecasting
Machine Learning.summary: In our experiments on long-horizon customer-behavior forecasting, a longer observation window outweighed the observed effects of more data, more capacity and newer architectures. The window is the weeks of history a model sees before the week it forecasts from. Going from an 8- to a 16-week window adds a raw +0.070 to 0.107 log-space $R^2$ in every family at 1M. Matched test cohorts, which score the same customer-weeks at every window, show this raw comparison understates the gain in every family they cover. The direction holds on five public datasets, four spanning over a year (ridge and our transformer on all five). On our internal data, longer windows admit up to 10% more and colder training customers, which matching does not fix. Our design does not separate window length from calendar coverage, because every test anchor (the week a forecast is made from) falls in one eight-week band. On training-period anchors, the weekly ridge probe's gain persists outside the holiday season, keeping about 72% of it. We therefore report a robust positive association with longer windows and do not identify the magnitude of a calendar-independent history effect. Of four internally registered predictions, the only fully blind one failed. An activity-mixture model predicted +0.014 from 24 to 32 weeks; the weekly-aggregate probe returned -0.0004. For the sequence families, the other three levers are about an order of magnitude smaller, bounded and unresolved. Their observed effects are at most 0.006 between the nominal 1M and 10M tiers and 0.0052 among five sequence families at 16 weeks with clocks as built, both single-seed on the full test split, and 0.006 for capacity on three-seed means. These are observed intervals, not equivalence bounds. Our claim is the order-of-magnitude contrast between the window and those bounds. A team building on this class of data should start by lengthening the window.

Machine Learning.title: Simple Private Noisy SGD is Minimax-Optimal under Population Strong Convexity
Machine Learning.summary: Stochastic gradient descent (SGD) is at the center of modern machine learning and is known to be statistically minimax-optimal in many regression settings, e.g., for convex Generalized Linear Models (GLMs). Yet, it is unknown whether its simplest differentially private Noisy SGD counterpart fulfills similar favorable guarantees even on strongly convex losses. We resolve this question affirmatively. We upper bound the parameter estimation error for a single pass of Noisy SGD with a fixed stepsize schedule and constant batch sizes on smooth and strongly convex Lipschitz losses over a compact convex domain under Renyi DP. Specialized to strongly convex GLMs, our error bounds match minimax lower bounds we derive based on the Score Attack framework. In particular, this provides the first minimax-optimal rate for Noisy SGD in private logistic regression, avoiding poly-logarithmic terms present in existing results. Our analysis is versatile as it relies on standard convex analysis and establishes the same rates in expectation and with high probability.

Machine Learning.title: Hybrid Retrieval for Government Scheme Search in English and Marathi
Machine Learning.summary: Retrieving government schemes requires matching citizens' information needs to formal administrative descriptions, often across languages and terminology. We present a bilingual search system for Maharashtra government schemes and public services that combines BM25 retrieval with sentence-embedding similarity through equal-weight score fusion. The system indexes aligned English-Marathi scheme descriptions and supports multilingual, Marathi-focused, and translation-mediated semantic configurations. Evaluation on manually curated bilingual queries compares BM25, dense retrieval, and hybrid retrieval using IndicSBERT and MahaSBERT. BM25 provides a strong baseline with a mean reciprocal rank (MRR) of 0.864. Hybrid retrieval increases MRR to 0.872 with IndicSBERT and 0.879 with MahaSBERT, whereas the corresponding dense-only systems achieve 0.663 and 0.655. MahaSBERT-based fusion also increases precision from 0.781 to 0.808 while matching BM25 recall at 0.946. These results support the complementary use of lexical and semantic signals in this collection, while showing that improvements over a strong lexical baseline are modest and metric-dependent. The study provides an application-focused analysis of hybrid retrieval for bilingual public-service information access.

Machine Learning.title: GroundAnything: Reconciling Parallel Decoding with Precise Visual Grounding at Flash Speed
Machine Learning.summary: Autoregressive (AR) grounding models serialize spatial predictions, introducing sequential latency and imposing a causal order on output tokens. We view grounding as visual evidence extraction: objects, locations, and spatial relations are jointly constrained by the image and query, yet their dependencies do not imply an intrinsic left-to-right generation order. This distinction makes bidirectional diffusion a natural fit, allowing spatial hypotheses to emerge in parallel and be jointly refined through iterative denoising. We introduce GroundAnything, a 4B-parameter grounding foundation model that reconciles fast parallel decoding with precise localization through blockwise denoising. Training combines grounding pretraining from public datasets and dedicated data engines, direct AR-to-diffusion conversion with joint AR and diffusion objectives, supervised fine-tuning, and GRPO-based reinforcement post-training. Across 30 grounding benchmarks, our autoregressive variant, GroundAnything-VLM, establishes a new overall state of the art among similarly sized models at 72.42%, remaining competitive with GPT-6 Astra (71.35%). With entropy-guided decoding, GroundAnything also surpasses the prior state of the art at this scale, averaging 61.75% versus 53.32% for the fast MTP-based LocateAnything model. We further explore decoding strategies, showing that an optional self-speculative mode achieves a 4.51$\times$ speedup over the AR counterpart with a 0.74 percentage-point drop in COCO F1mIoU. Infrastructure experiments show that progressive inference optimizations translate parallel decoding into practical speedups. These gains support efficient visual grounding in latency-sensitive real-world systems.

Machine Learning.title: Grid Cells as Spectral Successor Features: A Reusable Basis for Continual Reinforcement Learning
Machine Learning.summary: Continual reinforcement learning requires agents to adapt when the task changes while reusing what they know about the environment. Successor features separate dynamics from task-specific reward, but their effectiveness depends on the choice of base features. Taking the identification of entorhinal grid cells with eigenvectors of the successor representation as a design principle, we build this basis from eigenvectors of the transition matrix of a fixed reference policy. With such a basis, the successor features at a state-action pair are a linear combination of the base features at that same pair, which is not true in general, and the coefficients are known in closed form: each successor feature is its base feature multiplied by $θ_i = 1/(1-γλ_i)$, where $λ_i$ is its eigenvalue. The long-term return is thus predicted from the same features as the immediate reward, no successor-feature network or replay buffer is needed, and adapting to a new task reduces to a linear regression on the reward. The agent acts greedily on the action values of the reference policy, which is one step of policy improvement over it and suffices to reach a single goal. In a two-goal gridworld, with the uniform random walk as reference policy, whose eigenvectors are the low-frequency Laplacian eigenvectors, agents built this way maintain near-maximal return across every change of goal, whereas SimpleSF and DQN lose most of their return at each change.
Machine Learning.comment: 15 pages, 3 figures. Accepted at the NeurReps and WiML workshops at NeurIPS 2026

Machine Learning.title: Forecasting Patient Trajectories from the Electronic Health Records with Action-Conditioned World Models
Machine Learning.summary: We introduce a predictive world model for electronic health records (EHR) that represents patient histories as action conditioned latent trajectories. Rather than modeling clinical events solely through autoregressive token prediction, our framework explicitly separates patient states from observed clinical actions and learns their evolution through a state and action conditioned transition operator. At its core is a state dependent linearization predictor that propagates local changes in latent patient state, enabling time resolved prediction, multi step rollout, and action conditioned simulation. Empirically, we show that generated latent trajectories preserve downstream predictive signal, temporal structure, and subgroup level statistical relationships present in encoder derived representations. We further decode free running rollouts into the original clinical feature space and evaluate future clinical measurements against observed values using task matched forecasting baselines, demonstrating that the learned dynamics retain predictive information beyond latent space agreement. Across binary classification and time to event tasks, EHR WM achieves competitive, though task dependent, performance relative to substantially larger EHR foundation models while using a 30x smaller parameter footprint. Finally, perturbing observed action sequences produces corresponding changes in generated trajectories, demonstrating the action sensitivity of the learned dynamics. Together, these results support world modeling as a complementary framework for learning explicit, time indexed representations of patient evolution from longitudinal EHR.

Machine Learning.title: On Agentic Manipulation Policies
Machine Learning.summary: Recent work on robot manipulation has focused on specialist policies trained on demonstrations. We show that generalist AI models can control manipulators more reliably than specialist policies such as vision-language-action models (VLAs) and world-action models (WAMs). We systematically analyze agentic manipulation policies (AMPs), in which a generalist AI model commands the manipulator directly, adapting its actions as the task unfolds. We present AMP1, a reference harness that runs unchanged across single-arm, bimanual, and mobile manipulation. AMP1 achieves state-of-the-art results on the RoboLab-120 and CaP-Gym benchmarks, with no demonstrations or task-specific training. On RoboLab-120, AMP1 reaches an 85.6% success rate zero-shot, compared to 49.2% and 42.9% for leading VLA and WAM policies. The agent succeeds zero-shot in 104 of 108 real-world trials spanning twelve tasks and three robot instances, reducing failure rates by 20x and 15x relative to strong VLA and WAM baselines. The basic harness supplies no grasping, pushing, or placing skills; the agent develops its own strategies, such as searching for hidden objects, using objects as tools, and calibrating its cameras. With the addition of a persistent memory store, the agent can also learn from experience: an augmented harness with a memory representation that is carried across episodes lowers the failure rate on RoboDojo bimanual manipulation tasks by 4.6x relative to zero-shot deployment. Our analysis suggests that AMPs are substantially more general and robust than specialist manipulation policies, providing a promising foundation for robot manipulation. See https://apple-aiml-research.github.io/ml-amp/ for code and videos.

Machine Learning.title: Gravitational Duals from Equations of State II: Large Hierarchies and False Vacua
Machine Learning.summary: We investigate the reconstruction of holographic duals for strongly coupled quantum field theories in regimes characterized by large hierarchies and the presence of false vacua. Within the gauge/gravity duality, these features translate into non-trivial thermodynamic behaviour and exotic renormalization group flows, including skipping flows between non-adjacent fixed points. Building on previous work based on Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), we extend the holographic inverse problem of reconstructing the bulk scalar potential from boundary thermodynamic data into this new regime. This setting presents a variety of conceptual and numerical challenges, such as near-degenerate states, large hierarchies of energy scales, and regions of the potential that are not directly probed by the input data. We develop a set of methodological advances that overcome these obstacles, thereby improving the established PINNs-based methodology and extending it to new physical regimes of interest that were previously out of reach. Applying the developed framework, we demonstrate accurate reconstruction of scalar potentials deep into the false vacuum regime, achieving robust agreement with the physical features of the underlying thermodynamics despite significant numerical stiffness. Our results extend the bridge between holography and machine learning, and suggest that data-driven approaches can provide new insights into the structure of strongly coupled systems.

Machine Learning.title: Anticipating Future Build Results with BuildPredictor
Machine Learning.summary:
Continuous Integration (CI) is a popular programming practice for the seamless integration of code changes into the code base. Using CI, developers benefit from automated assembling and testing of the code after each commit. However, while the frequent integration and building supports developers, it also comes at the high costs of wasting time and resources for minimal changes.
  In this work, we investigate the potential of reducing the drawbacks by anticipating the build outcome using machine learning techniques. In particular, we propose a random forest model with various features such as changes to the source and build code, and changes to the complexity of the code.
  We observe that our model shows a good performance in an intra-project and holistic setting yielding a median MCC of 0.82 and 0.86, respectively. We also found that the most important features of our model concern the historical build result information. Additionally, we investigated the development of the performance of our model over time and found that our model can quickly arrive at its peak performance.
  In an additional experiment, we removed the hard-to-interpret historical build information features and found that our model still yields decent performance while improving the interpretability of it. Summarizing, our model can help to avoid unnecessary build runs by anticipating the build result and thus, save resources.

Machine Learning.title: A new algorithmic approach for finding flat minima: critically damped Polyak stepsizes
Machine Learning.summary: We present a new adaptive stepsize rule that biases gradient descent toward flatter minima in both theory and practice, and establish the first uniform-in-time guarantees for both sharpness and loss reduction for a broad class of locally quadratic objectives. Our critically damped Polyak (CDP) stepsizes multiply the classical Polyak rule by $4$ and a mild damping factor. The factor $4$ is critical in that it produces equioscillations around the manifold of minimizers $\mathcal{M}$ to leading order. Damping provably drives convergence to $\mathcal{M}$. CDP thus operates at the edge of stability by adapting its stepsizes to local curvature. Once the loss is small, its projected iterates follow gradient descent on $\log{λ_1(\nabla^2 \mathcal{L})}$ along $\mathcal{M}$ to leading order, paralleling the flatness bias of normalized gradient descent (Arora et al., 2022). Unlike normalized gradient descent, CDP step lengths shrink with the distance to $\mathcal{M}$, enabling convergence to an interpolating solution that locally minimizes sharpness at finite learning rate. We establish our theory for a broad class of non-negative losses with locally quadratic Morse-Bott structure near $\mathcal{M}$, capturing regular interpolation regimes in smooth overparameterized neural networks. Empirically, CDP stepsizes produce a flattening effect similar to that of Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM, Foret et al., 2021), reducing sharpness even in settings beyond our theory, including nonlinear teacher-student networks and fine-tuning of pre-trained LLMs.

Machine Learning.title: Extensions of Robbins-Siegmund Theorem with Applications in Reinforcement Learning
Machine Learning.summary: The Robbins-Siegmund theorem establishes the convergence of stochastic processes that are almost supermartingales and is one of the most commonly used approaches for analyzing stochastic iterative algorithms in stochastic approximation and reinforcement learning (RL). However, its original form has a significant limitation as it requires the zero-order term to be summable. In many important RL applications, this summable condition, however, cannot be met. This limitation motivates us to extend the Robbins-Siegmund theorem for almost supermartingales where the zero-order term is not summable, but only square-summable. In particular, we introduce a novel and mild assumption on the increments of the stochastic processes. This together with the square-summable condition enables an almost sure convergence to a bounded set. Additionally, we further provide almost sure convergence rates, high probability concentration bounds, and $L^p$ convergence rates. We then apply the new results to stochastic approximation and RL. Notably, we obtain the first almost sure convergence rate, the first high probability concentration bound, and the first $L^p$ convergence rate for $Q$-learning with linear function approximation.

Machine Learning.title: STEPQuant: When and Where Errors Matter in Delta-Rule Recurrent State Quantization
Machine Learning.summary: Linear attention replaces growing KV caches with fixed-size recurrent states, yet these persistent states can become a substantial memory bottleneck under concurrent serving. Directly quantizing recurrent states to low precision often leads to severe accuracy degradation, as quantization errors propagate through successive state updates. We discover that the impact of these errors depends on two complementary dimensions: temporally, errors in long-lived memory can persist across many decoding steps; spatially, errors in different key rows affect model outputs differently, while state magnitudes vary substantially along both rows and columns. Motivated by these observations, we propose STEPQuant, a spatial-temporal post-training quantization framework for Delta-rule recurrent states. STEPQuant allocates precision according to error magnitude and memory lifetime, and jointly fits key-row and value-column scales based on state distributions and key-row impact on output error. Experiments on Qwen3.8-27B and Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct across both long- and short-generation benchmarks show that STEPQuant closely matches FP32-state accuracy under a nominal 6-bit budget and outperforms uniform INT8 in its 4-bit configuration. Integrated into SGLang with optimized GPU kernels, 6-bit STEPQuant achieves over 5x recurrent-state compression and reduces total serving memory by up to 68.7%. Our code is available at https://github.com/Dreamer-Toby/STEPQuant.
Machine Learning.comment: Technical report; v2: Expanded experiments and evaluations

Machine Learning.title: A Bayesian latent class reinforcement learning framework to capture adaptive, feedback-driven travel behaviour
Machine Learning.summary: Many travel decisions involve a degree of experience formation, where individuals learn their preferences over time. At the same time, there is extensive scope for heterogeneity across individual travellers, both in their underlying preferences and in how these evolve. The present paper puts forward a Latent Class Reinforcement Learning (LCRL) model that allows analysts to capture both of these phenomena. We apply the model to a driving simulator dataset and estimate the parameters through Variational Bayes. We identify three distinct classes of individuals that differ markedly in how they adapt their preferences: the first displays context-dependent preferences with context-specific exploitative tendencies; the second follows a persistent exploitative strategy regardless of context; and the third engages in an exploratory strategy combined with context-specific preferences.

Machine Learning.title: Neural Conditional Gaussian Model: Efficient Data Assimilation with Sequential Uncertainty Quantification for Nonlinear Dynamics
Machine Learning.summary: Data assimilation (DA) in partially observed nonlinear systems requires repeated estimation of both hidden states and their uncertainty. Conventional nonlinear filtering can be computationally expensive and often relies on an explicit dynamical model. In this paper, we develop the Neural Conditional Gaussian Model (Neural CGM), a data-driven dynamical model that maps unobserved physical states into a learned latent space, where the dynamics of the latent states follow a conditional Gaussian structure. This structure allows closed-form DA updates in the latent space, while nonlinear encoder-decoder mappings retain the flexibility needed to represent complex dynamics in physical space. A key feature of Neural CGM is its treatment of uncertainty in DA. The latent posterior mean and covariance are mapped to the physical variables through a Gaussian decoder that combines local moment propagation with learned nonlinear corrections. The resulting physical-space posterior statistics depend on the sequentially updated latent distribution rather than on a separate post-processing estimate. The same statistics enter a Gaussian negative log-likelihood during training, so both the posterior mean and uncertainty affect the learned model. Because Neural CGM learns the dynamical model itself, it can also be used for state forecasting and simulation without explicit knowledge of the governing equations. Numerical experiments on benchmark nonlinear dynamical systems show accurate state estimation and forecasting while substantially reducing online assimilation cost relative to conventional nonlinear DA methods. Neural CGM is therefore suited to repeated state estimation, uncertainty quantification, and prediction from partial observations.

Machine Learning.title: Bayesian optimization on amortized search space
Machine Learning.summary: In real-world black-box optimization problems, a mechanistic simulator is often available that approximately predicts the behavior of the system as a function of the parameters being optimized. Here, we show how an amortized inverse map of such a simulator can be used in Bayesian optimization to restrict the search space while using a Gaussian process kernel that is aware of the original problem geometry. This allows for efficiently leveraging the low intrinsic dimensionality of the optimization problem. We characterize its approximation bias and information gain, and derive an intrinsic-dimension-dependent regret rate under additional geometric and Gaussian Process assumptions. We illustrate the method with an application to drug dosing personalization in Parkinson's disease. We use, as a simulator, a pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) model of a drug, a mechanistic model calibrated on population data with quantified parameter uncertainty. A dosing neural network is trained offline against the model, amortizing the map from patient PK/PD parameters to the regimen predicted to be optimal, and online Bayesian optimization then searches over this learned, low-dimensional representation rather than over raw dosages. Numerical simulations demonstrate the improved performance of our method in this application, as well as under simulator misspecification.

Machine Learning.title: Chameleon: Dynamic Format Adapter for Efficient Diffusion
Machine Learning.summary: Post-training quantization (PTQ) is the standard way to run modern diffusion models on memory-constrained accelerators, yet every existing diffusion PTQ scheme fixes the $\mathit{number\ format}$ in advance and only tunes the scale, zero point, or per-layer bit-width. At a fixed bit-width the best format depends on the distribution being encoded, and that distribution differs across weight channels, across layers, and along the diffusion timestep, where activation distributions slide from heavy-tailed and noise-dominated to tightly clustered and structured. We propose Chameleon, a PTQ framework that holds the bit-width fixed and treats the format itself as a discrete variable, chosen per weight channel and per activation layer, optionally refined per timestep bucket. Activation formats come from {INT8, FP8 E4M3, FP8 E5M2, MXFP8, MXINT8}, selected ahead of time from two cheap statistics (empirical kurtosis and the closed-form diffusion SNR) and stored in a lookup table; weight formats come from {INT8, MXINT8} at 8 bits or {INT4, NF4, FP4 E2M1, MXINT4, MXFP4} at 4 bits, selected offline by reconstruction error. An architectural fork adapts the same selection layer to multi-step UNets, single-step distilled models, and Diffusion Transformers. Most of the gain comes from the per-layer choice; the timestep refinement helps mainly at 6-bit activations. Across SDXL, SDXL-Turbo, and PixArt-$α$ on COCO-2014, Chameleon achieves the best FID in all six backbone $\times$ bit-width settings, with CLIP within 0.24 of the FP16 reference and the best of all quantized methods at $W_{4}A_{8}$. On PixArt-$α$, a real mixed-format kernel runs 1.09$\times$ faster than FP16 end-to-end with 3$\times$ smaller weights.

Machine Learning.title: Scaling classical hardware for accurate real-time quantum error correction
Machine Learning.summary: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires a classical decoder fast enough to process syndrome measurements at the rate at which they are generated, and to return its decisions with low latency. This is most demanding for superconducting processors, whose fast syndrome cycles force a trade-off between decoding speed and accuracy. Decoders fast enough to keep up sacrifice accuracy, which must be compensated for with larger codes and thus additional physical qubits. Here we introduce Rapids, a streaming neural decoder that is both fast and accurate. We achieve this by co-designing the decoder with a field-programmable gate array (FPGA): the network is built from operations that map cheaply onto the device and trained in its integer arithmetic. For the distance-19 surface code, Rapids decodes each round of syndromes in under a microsecond on a single FPGA, fast enough for superconducting processors, and returns its decisions with the low latency that fault-tolerant algorithms require. Its logical error rate is 240 times lower than that of existing real-time hardware decoders. The same design extends to the color code and the [[144,12,12]] bivariate-bicycle code, on which our decoder is 16 times more accurate than the real-time Relay decoder. We further show that the decoder scales: spread over several FPGAs or hardened into custom silicon, it becomes faster, more accurate, or able to decode larger codes. Classical hardware thus becomes a further resource, alongside qubits, that can be scaled to improve fault-tolerant quantum computers.
Machine Learning.comment: 13 pages, 5 figures, 4 Extended Data figures, 1 Extended Data table

Machine Learning.title: Stop Removing Stopwords: How an Inherited Preprocessing Default Distorts Legal Text-as-Data
Machine Learning.summary: Empirical legal scholarship increasingly treats judicial text as data, and much of it still runs on sparse, interpretable pipelines -- TF-IDF features and linear classifiers -- because the textual feature is often the object of study rather than a means to prediction. Yet these pipelines inherit preprocessing defaults from mid-century information retrieval that were never validated against classification accuracy. The most entrenched of these is stopword removal. This study introduces an exhaustive single word ablation that measures the effect of a preprocessing step directly against the downstream objective, and applies it to stopword removal as the hardest case to dislodge. Matching Supreme Court Database labels to Caselaw Access Project opinion texts, the study examines two binary tasks that bracket F1 headroom, ideological direction (no-removal baseline F1 ~0.68) and constitutional versus non-constitutional law type (~0.92), across 7,668 and 7,001 opinions. For each task, the ablation removes each of about 18,500 candidate words in turn, and a task-specific stoplist is built from the measurements. Common generic stoplists fall below the no-removal baseline in all twelve held-out tests. The task-specific stoplists move held-out F1 by +0.0023 (95% CI [-0.0124, +0.0170]) on ideology and by +0.0001 ([-0.0082, +0.0085]) on law type. Neither task shows a detectable benefit from removal, and supplemental analysis finds that word-level statistics predict removal effects poorly, because true removal effects differ by less than the measurement can register, leaving little to predict. The method generalizes to any inherited preprocessing default; the result is a caution specific to interpretable legal text-as-data, where a step that reshapes which features a model sees can distort the doctrinal and ideological signal the research is meant to recover. The burden of proof sits with removal.

Machine Learning.title: Should Belgians Install an Advanced Energy Management System in Their Electrified Dwelling ?
Machine Learning.summary:
As dwellings electrify and more complex electricity pricing spreads in Belgium, the question arises: What are the potential benefits of installing an advanced energy management systems in an electrified Belgian dwelling ?
  To answer this question, we simulate 500 representative Belgian dwellings in which fossil systems are replaced by controllable electric technologies: space heating via air-to-air heat pumps, domestic hot water via electric boilers, and private transport via electric vehicles with home chargers. Photovoltaic systems are assigned according to current adoption rates.
  We evaluate two advanced energy management systems (EMS): model predictive control (MPC) and TreeC, a machine learning method using decision trees to model the EMS strategy. These are compared to a rule-based controller (RBC) that mimics default operation and an MPC with perfect forecasts (MPC P) as an upper bound. Performance for these EMSs is assessed for 2023 under a real contract with hourly prices and a monthly peak tariff.
  Average annual savings versus RBC are 82.5 EUR, 116.6 EUR, and 177.4 EUR for TreeC, MPC, and MPC P, respectively. All EMSs deliver similar thermal comfort (26-31 Kh). MPC saves more, while TreeC achieves higher EV charge completion (93.3% vs 88.8% for MPC, with a max charge of 95%) and a smoother aggregate load across the 500 dwellings. Savings remain modest relative to EMS purchase (280-680 EUR) and subscription (0-360 EUR/year) costs which is not favourable towards widespread adoption.
  The data and code to reproduce this study are available at https://github.com/EVERGi/should_belgians_install_advanced_ems_paper.
Machine Learning.comment: Full version including appendices A-C, which are not part of the 11-page proceedings version. Published at ACM BuildSys '26 under CC BY 4.0. 17 pages, 10 figures, 13 tables. Data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18417982

Machine Learning.title: The sublevel Flood bifiltration: towards scalable 2-parameter persistent homology
Machine Learning.summary: Multiparameter persistent homology is a rapidly developing branch of topological data analysis that improves the robustness of single-parameter persistent homology to outliers, while still capturing the metric characteristics of the data. However, a notable limitation is its lack of scalability. In this paper, we introduce a novel approach for efficiently computing 2-parameter persistent homology on large point sets. Our work extends the Flood filtration, originally developed for single-parameter persistence. Our construction, called the sublevel Flood bifiltration, offers a scalable approximation of the sublevel offset bifiltration. We show that it benefits from theoretical stability properties and describe how to compute it efficiently. We demonstrate the performance of our approach in classification tasks on low-dimensional synthetic datasets, where density awareness is critical, as well as on real-world time series datasets.

Machine Learning.title: Learning to Defer under Expert Drift
Machine Learning.summary: The learning to defer (L2D) framework enables safety in machine learning and AI systems by allocating difficult or critical decisions to a human expert. However, most prior work on L2D assumes fixed expert reliability, overlooking temporal fluctuations in human performance due to factors such as fatigue and cognitive biases. Humans commonly exhibit such substantial, systematic performance shifts across a wide range of domains, from high-stakes settings such as radiology, aviation, and judicial decision-making, to everyday tasks such as crowdsourced image annotation. We propose Expert-Drift-Adapted Learning-to-Defer (EDA-L2D), a novel expert-aware L2D framework that explicitly models these temporal shifts by conditioning the deferral head on recent histories of expert outcomes via a sequence model. This history-aware approach enables adaptive deferral policies that anticipate reliability fluctuations and better allocate decisions between human and machine over time. We provide comprehensive experiments across three diverse tasks -- image classification, medical diagnosis, and hate speech detection -- including generalization analyses under realistic deferral conditions and irregular shifts in expert reliability. Our results show that EDA-L2D adapts more effectively than prior L2D methods to diverse temporal patterns of expert reliability, resulting in improved system performance and more effective deferral decisions. Code is available at https://github.com/ZiyaoMou/L2D-Expert-Drift.

Machine Learning.title: Synthetic Neurosymbolic Task Generation with Controlled Constraint Complexity
Machine Learning.summary:
We introduce NeSySy, a synthetic generator for neurosymbolic learning tasks that jointly produces logical constraints and consistent datasets. Unlike existing benchmarks, NeSySy provides fine-grained control over key properties such as constraint structure, tightness, input dependence, and data generation and alignment strategies. In particular, it allows the use of rich constraints over infinite domains, and uses solvers to ensure that the constraints are meaningful and that generated samples satisfy the constraints.
  We design NeSySy to support both learning with declarative constraints and learning from distant supervision. Across a range of constraint families, we provide evidence that its parameters induce systematic and largely independent effects on task difficulty. Using NeSySy, we study constraint-aware learning methods, identifying regimes where explicit constraint enforcement is beneficial and where expressive unconstrained models can instead learn constraint structure directly from data. Our results establish NeSySy as a controlled testbed for analysing the interaction between learning and logical structure.
  NeSySy is built around a pipeline that incorporates solvers. Satisfiability checkers (CNFgen and Z3) generate and certify constraints. Constrained optimizers (RC2 for MaxSAT, Z3 for OMT) compute optimal repairs that guarantee every generated sample is consistent.

Machine Learning.title: Exact Bayesian layers via characteristic functions
Machine Learning.summary: Bayesian neural networks provide principled uncertainty estimates, but training them with Monte Carlo sampling can be expensive. Sampling-free variational inference algorithms make training Bayesian neural networks feasible, but existing approaches assume a Gaussian output distribution, which can be inaccurate in applied problems. Here, we introduce CF-Prop, an uncertainty propagation method that uses characteristic functions to compute the exact output distribution of a Bayesian ReLU layer, without any sampling, even in non-Gaussian settings. Because CF-Prop propagates characteristic functions, the evidence lower bound---the objective of variational training---can be computed in closed form for a broad class of likelihoods, including the Gaussian, Poisson, and Gamma. This allows to implement an efficient resulting variational inference algorithm, CF-VI. On CIFAR-100, CF-VI achieves the lowest calibration error of any tested method, improving on the next best method by about 35%. On a heavy-tailed insurance claim dataset, CF-VI accurately captures tail uncertainty that is severely underestimated by both other sampling-free methods and Monte Carlo methods.

Machine Learning.title: FEA solver integration of a composite World Model with a Spiking Neural Network memory Block for computationally efficient modelling of defects and variabilities
Machine Learning.summary: Each fibre-reinforced composite structure has a unique material architecture. The manufacturing methods used and the presence of defects lead to local variations which require material-scale models that can resolve the response in real time at every location in the structure. Concurrent multi-scale schemes provide this capability, but at a prohibitive computational cost for large structures as the number of integration points and time increments scales with size. Surrogates have been studied extensively as replacements for material-scale models to mitigate these computational limitations. A surrogate must represent an arbitrary local architecture including defects, track the irreversible material state over an unknown number of increments, remain stable when driven recursively by its own predictions, and fit within the memory available at every integration point. Here, a Composites World Model based on a Multi-Modal Spiking Transformer architecture is designed to meet these requirements. The proposed architecture combines a material encoder, a Spiking Neural Network memory block that tracks the long-term internal state of the material, and transformer blocks that learn the short-term applied strain state. The system is trained in three stages: material architecture encoding, base training on short time windows, and recursive fine-tuning with scheduled sampling to suppress cumulative error drift. The trained model is disassembled at inference and coupled to a non-linear FE solver, enabling structural scale simulation of composites containing embedded defects. Benchmarks against experimental results for IM7/8552 laminates under tension, compression and transverse shear, for pristine and wrinkled composites, show that the SNN memory block successfully tracks the material internal state and results in prediction errors between 0.4% and 4.8%.

Machine Learning.title: Sequential Anytime Valid Tests for Efficient Inference-Time Alignment
Machine Learning.summary: Inference-time alignment methods, such as Best-of-N (BoN), improve language model outputs by generating multiple candidates per prompt and selecting among them using a reward model. Much of this cost is wasted: a fixed budget is applied to every prompt, although the computation required by prompts varies widely. Adaptive methods halt once sampled answers appear settled, but their thresholds are tuned heuristics with no statistical control over early-stopping errors. We instead seek an anytime-valid stopping rule that takes an error tolerance $α$ as input and halts only once an answer is certified to hold a majority ($θ_a > 1/2$) under the generator's distribution. We aggregate candidates by final answer with a reward-weighted self-consistency (RWSC) score and treat stopping as a sequential test over the resulting clusters. Applying Wald's sequential probability ratio test to these clusters yields SPRT-RWSC, which performs well empirically, but its guarantee fails because the leading answer shifts during sampling, and the run is continuously monitored. Our main contribution, e-RWSC, replaces Wald's test with a betting supermartingale (an e-process) for every answer the policy produces, bounding the probability of ever certifying a non-dominant answer by $α$, uniformly over time and across all answers. The RWSC scores drive the bets, so they affect only how quickly a dominant answer $a^\star$ is certified, not validity; certification takes $O(\log(1/α)/d_{\mathrm{KL}}(θ_{a^\star}\|1/2))$ samples. Experiments across several language models, datasets, and reward models confirm the predicted $1/d_{\mathrm{KL}}$ scaling of cost and show that accuracy improves over baselines at substantially lower token cost.

Machine Learning.title: How to Effectively Manage the Energy in Residential Systems: Development and Comparison of Methods
Machine Learning.summary:
The transition from fossil fuels presents significant challenges in energy management. To ensure a sustainable energy future, it is crucial to reduce energy consumption when possible and to synchronize electricity consumption and storage with the production from sources with low greenhouse gas emissions. This thesis explores a variety of energy management methods used to manage batteries, heat pumps, and other energy-related systems. The thesis presents three simulation cases alongside one real-world experiment to compare energy management done through simple rules, optimization, and machine learning methods. Furthermore, this thesis introduces TreeC, a novel machine learning-based method that learns understandable yet efficient energy management strategies, applicable to many cases.
  The three key contributions of this thesis can be summarized as follows: 1) The developed TreeC method demonstrates competitive performance compared to a variety of energy management approaches, such as model predictive control and reinforcement learning, across a diverse set of energy management problems. The understandability of TreeC's energy management strategies greatly improves the transparency and trustworthiness of machine learning-based energy management. 2) The real-world experiment highlights the need to validate energy management methods on actual hardware and not solely on simulations. Both TreeC and model predictive control performed worse than in simulations, due to, respectively, insufficiently representative training data and the real-time input data not being reliable enough. 3) Energy management algorithms reduce costs in electrified Belgian dwellings, particularly in poorly insulated dwellings, electric vehicle chargers, and photovoltaic installations. However, on average, these cost savings do not yet outweigh the current costs and effort required to implement such algorithms.

Machine Learning.title: The Dichotomy Between Pattern Recognition and Step-by-Step Reasoning
Machine Learning.summary: We argue that pattern recognition and step-by-step reasoning are two ends of a spectrum. A large language model (LLM) learns to reason step-by-step when data is structured such that the next token depends on a small amount of preceding context. Inference in LLMs resembles pattern recognition when the next token depends on a large amount of preceding context. If the next token depends on only the $c$ most recent tokens, reasoning traces are paths on a de Bruijn graph whose nodes are $c$-length contexts and edges are next-token transitions between contexts. The set of reasoning traces of a task forms a directed acyclic subgraph of the de Bruijn graph. An LLM that has learned all edges of this subgraph can compose them to solve longer, unseen tasks, i.e., it reasons step-by-step. We prove that the number of edges is vanishingly small compared to the number of reasoning traces. We also prove and show empirically that the number of training samples a transformer needs is a linear in the number of edges, so learning to reason step-by-step is sample efficient. We can induce de Bruijn structure in any task by maintaining a ``state'' that makes future reasoning independent of the past. The frequency of states in the reasoning trace determines $c$. We show, by fine-tuning Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct to solve equations and answer questions about stories, that frequent states (small $c$) result in higher accuracy but greater fragility to perturbations at test time. LLMs trained with a large $c$ are only as good as models that perform pattern recognition without reasoning. A moderate density of states balances accuracy and robustness. Real-world data has de Bruijn structure: Qwen3-14B and Qwen3-32B retain over 75\% of their accuracy on GSM8K, MATH-500 and GPQA-Diamond when attention is restricted to a sliding window less than 15\% as long as the full reasoning trace.

Machine Learning.title: Statistical Inference with Ill-Conditioned Random Weight Neural Network Sieves
Machine Learning.summary: Random weight neural networks (RWNNs) are shallow networks whose hidden-layer parameters are randomly generated and then kept fixed, while only the output coefficients are estimated. Conditional on the sampled parameters, RWNN regression is a linear sieve problem with random approximation space. We show that such random sieves cannot remain uniformly well-conditioned as their dimension grows. For parametrized feature families satisfying polynomial covering and Lipschitz conditions, the eigenvalues of the population covariance matrix are proven to have polynomial upper bounds determined by the covering geometry of the parameter space, leading to a vanishing smallest eigenvalue. We develop approximation, estimation, and inference theory that explicitly treats the ill-conditioning. Under a $β$-Hölder source condition, we obtain both faster-than-Monte-Carlo $L^2$ approximation rates and new $L^\infty$ approximation bounds based on stratified sampling. We then derive improved consistency guarantees for ridge-regularized least squares driven by ridge effective dimension, spectral, and leverage-based stability conditions. For inference, we establish asymptotic linearity and Gaussian limits for linear functional directions while allowing the smallest eigenvalue of the population covariance matrix to vanish. Nondegeneracy is directional: we characterize it with a ridge-normalized Rayleigh quotient and extend it to smooth functionals via Riesz representation. Consistency of ridge-adjusted variance estimators is proved, yielding feasible studentized inference. Numerical experiments illustrate the deterioration of random-feature conditioning and the finite-sample behavior of the resulting estimation and inference procedures.

Machine Learning.title: Déjà Cue: Localizing States in Object Histories via Vocabulary-Relative Coordinates
Machine Learning.summary: Object tracking preserves identity through visual changes, but cannot tell when an object is whole, cut, or peeled. We study state-moment retrieval: locating when a tracked object exhibits each state in a supplied set of descriptions. However, absolute image--text similarity can favor shared object semantics, obscuring the distinctions needed to localize individual states. Our insight is that the alternatives themselves provide a reference for measuring state evidence. We introduce Déjà Cue, a training-free framework that centers description embeddings on a state-balanced vocabulary mean, producing query directions that compare each state against its alternatives. Using frozen vision--language encoders, Déjà Cue calibrates frame scores and retrieves intervals at multiple durations within contiguous visible runs. We construct MS-VOST by annotating 620 object histories with 2,465 states. With the encoder and temporal search fixed, Déjà Cue improves all three localization metrics over absolute scoring across eight encoder configurations, raising Top-1 temporal IoU by 0.42--1.14 percentage points. These gains persist across four text constructions, and candidate-ranking analysis shows that the vocabulary reference brings relevant intervals forward within the same search space. These results establish the supplied state vocabulary as an object-specific reference for localizing semantic states from frozen visual representations.

Machine Learning.title: Flow Matching from Non-Gaussian Sources: A Theory of Efficient Sampling
Machine Learning.summary: Flow matching is a versatile framework for generative modeling that transports a source distribution to a target data distribution. A key advantage is its flexibility in the choice of source distribution, such as heavy-tailed and multimodal sources. Yet finite-step sampling guarantees for non-Gaussian sources remain limited. We establish a nonasymptotic convergence theory for Euler discretization of flow matching with linear interpolation. Suppose the source distribution on $\mathbb{R}^d$ has an everywhere positive, continuously differentiable density, finite total variance $\mathsf{TotVar}_{\mathsf{base}}$, and an $L$-Lipschitz score. Using the population velocity field and a suitable time grid, this sampler achieves total variation error at most $\varepsilon$ in $\widetilde{O}(Ld\mathsf{TotVar}_{\mathsf{base}}/\varepsilon)$ iterations, provided the target distribution satisfies a mild second-moment condition. These assumptions cover, among many examples, source distributions such as multivariate Student's $t$ distributions with more than two degrees of freedom and finite Gaussian mixtures with shared covariance, while accommodating target distributions with neither a smooth density nor bounded support.

Machine Learning.title: Balance of Benchmarks: Evidence Retention and Multiplicity-Aware Model Comparison
Machine Learning.summary: Benchmark aggregation requires decisions about how much evidence to use and how much influence each benchmark receives. Curated suites control influence through selection, which can exclude informative observations. A broader pool can retain those observations. With equal weighting, repeated or closely related benchmarks gain influence as their number grows. We introduce Balance of Benchmarks (BoB) to retain eligible observations and control their influence separately. We fit benchmark-specific response curves to place different difficulty ranges on a shared ability scale and use description similarity to downweight benchmarks in crowded neighborhoods. We test retention and density weighting in separate interventions on WildScores, a sparse collection of 148 developer-reported benchmarks, using 14 Artificial Analysis benchmarks as a controlled reference. With the model population fixed and entire source-lineage families held out, suite expansion improves held-out prediction under BoB and equal-weight equating on both WildScores and BIG-bench. Under substantial reporting overlap, density weighting improves robustness to multiplicity. Complete re-listings yield smaller mean rank displacement under BoB (0.63 versus 1.95 for equal-weight equating), with benefits also in paraphrased re-listings and supported affine fits. The benefit can reverse if models report different benchmarks, because a single weight per column gives models that report only part of a group less than its intended share. We therefore compute each model's weights from the benchmarks it reports. This rule removes the reversal in controlled re-listings and keeps held-out prediction close to that of equal weighting. These comparisons separate evidence retention, benchmark influence, and reporting coverage and show why repeated entries need to be handled per model.

Machine Learning.title: Privacy-Utility Tradeoffs with Quantum Local Differential Privacy
Machine Learning.summary: When sensitive information is encoded in data, it is important to ensure the privacy of information when attempting to learn useful information from the data. There is a natural tradeoff whereby increasing privacy requirements may decrease the utility of a learning protocol. In the quantum setting of differential privacy, such tradeoffs between privacy and utility have so far remained largely unexplored. In this work, we study optimal privacy-utility tradeoffs for both generic and application-specific utility metrics when privacy is quantified by $(\varepsilon,δ)$-quantum local differential privacy. In the generic setting, we focus on optimizing fidelity and trace distance between the original state and the privatized state. We show that the depolarizing mechanism achieves the optimal utility for given privacy requirements. We then study the specific application of learning the expectation of an observable with respect to an input state when only given access to privatized states. We derive a lower bound on the number of samples of privatized data required to achieve a fixed accuracy guarantee with high probability. To prove this result, we employ existing lower bounds on private quantum hypothesis testing, thus showcasing the first operational use of them. We also devise private mechanisms that achieve optimal sample complexity with respect to the privacy parameters and accuracy parameters, demonstrating that utility can be significantly improved for specific tasks in contrast to the generic setting. In addition, we show that the number of samples required to privately learn observable expectation values scales as $Θ((\varepsilon β)^{-2})$, where $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$ is the privacy parameter and $β$ is the accuracy tolerance. We conclude by initiating the study of private classical shadows, which promise useful applications for private learning tasks.
Machine Learning.comment: v2:accepted to Quantum Science and Technology, November 2026, 25pages; v1:23 pages, 2 figures

Machine Learning.title: Simulation-pretrained autoencoders versus PCA for compressing multimode fibre transmission matrices
Machine Learning.summary: Multimode optical fibres can image through a thin, flexible probe once their transmission matrix (TM) has been measured, but a TM is large and must be re-measured whenever the fibre moves. A compact model of feasible TMs would make storing and re-estimating them cheaper, so we ask how compactly TMs can be represented, and from how few measured TMs. Here we benchmark a permutation-equivariant autoencoder, pretrained on simulated fibres and adapted to measured TMs, against principal component analysis (PCA). At 62x compression, adapting the pretrained autoencoder with just two measured TMs reconstructs the TM of a 50um fibre well enough to focus light at 98% of the ideal enhancement, and it stays accurate when the TMs are shifted by 25 pixels or zoomed by 10%, which quickly degrades a linear basis. It is not, however, a better compressor: PCA is about ten times more accurate when fitted on all 163 real TMs (1.1% against 11.9% error on held-out TMs) and is already more accurate from ten. The autoencoder's value is as a prior when few or no real TMs exist: with none it reaches 29% error, against 91% for PCA fitted on the same simulation. Transfer to a different fibre is only partial. The most important extension, not yet tested, is to recover pixel-basis TMs from fewer measurements than a full TM, which would turn the pretrained prior from a compressor into a measurement-saving tool.

Machine Learning.title: A Complete Geometric Message-Passing Architecture for Point Clouds
Machine Learning.summary:
Three-dimensional point clouds are a fundamental data modality, and a large family of machine learning architectures has been developed to respect their natural symmetries to rigid motions and permutations. A principled way to compare these architectures, which vary widely in complexity and cost, is through their expressive power. That is, an architecture is complete if it can distinguish any two inputs not related by the symmetries it respects. Simple distance-based message-passing networks are known to be incomplete, and while there exist complete alternatives, they typically rely on computationally intensive mechanisms like high-order representations of the rotation group or higher-order Weisfeiler-Leman-type tests.
  In this work, we devise a novel, simple, equivariant message-passing architecture for point clouds, and prove that it is complete. We complement our theoretical result with experiments showing that our architecture separates challenging point clouds that distance-based message passing provably cannot distinguish. Our results suggest that high-order equivariant features may not be necessary to enhance the expressivity of point cloud architectures, and can help settle completeness for other equivariant architectures for which such results are currently unknown. We give initial evidence for this by proving completeness of a slightly modified version of SEGNN.
Machine Learning.comment: 44 pages, 4 figures, 4 tables. Ancillary files: exact-arithmetic verifier, certificate and companion notebook for the Platonic color-atom computation

Machine Learning.title: Evidence from a Multi-Regime Causal Discovery Benchmark: UCMT Algorithms, Comparative Performance, and Controlled Ablation Studies
Machine Learning.summary: We present an internal, pre-registered evaluation of the UCMT causal discovery algorithm family alongside established alternatives across heterogeneous benchmark regimes, complemented by a separately pre-registered, controlled study of UCMT v2 Global components. The contribution is both empirical and methodological: a family-stratified comparison of three actively developed algorithm configurations and targeted evidence about which internal stages affect their outcomes. In the main benchmark, UCMT v2 Global has higher directed F1 than NOTEARS and DAGMA in selected real, semi-synthetic and Gaussian-network comparisons at the paired-run level, while trailing leading permutation-search methods in other settings. The BOSS-based UCMT v4 produces a CSuite-specific directed-F1 improvement over BOSS (mean paired difference +0.279; pair-level Holm p < 0.001), but the dataset-level adjusted result is not significant (p = 0.188). In a separate fixed-skeleton ablation, UCMT v2 Global exceeds an adapted R^2-SortnRegress orientation baseline on standardized iSCM data (directed F1 0.537 vs 0.468, dataset-level Holm p = 0.031); absolute orientation accuracy is 0.563 and there is no established broad advantage over RESIT, ANM or DirectLiNGAM. Controlled ablations show that sparsity and BIC-based refinement materially affect some outcomes, whereas the examined arbitration and automatic regime-selection mechanisms do not yield confirmed general improvements. We report performance shortcomings, multiple-testing correction, runtime costs, evaluation limitations and reproducibility checks. The results support UCMT as an implemented and empirically investigated algorithm family, not a claim of overall superiority, independent validation or demonstrated commercial impact.
Machine Learning.comment: 8 pages, 4 figures, 6 tables. Internal benchmark and controlled ablation study; not peer-reviewed

Machine Learning.title: TriAxialKV: Toward Extreme Low-Precision KV-Cache Quantization for Agentic Inference Tasks
Machine Learning.summary: Agentic workloads have emerged as a major workload for LLM inference. They differ significantly from chat-only workloads, requiring long-context processing, the ability to handle multimodal inputs, and structured multi-turn interactions with tool calling capabilities. As a result, their context exhibits structure that can carry different importance along three key axes: temporal recency to the current turn, modality such as text or image tokens, and semantic role such as user queries, tool calls, observations, or reasoning. These axes capture distinct token behaviors and lead to different sensitivities to KV-cache compression. However, existing KV-cache quantization methods are typically homogeneous or exploit only heterogeneity on a single dimension, such as temporal proximity or modality, overlooking the interactions among them. To this end, we introduce TriAxialKV, a novel mixed-precision KV-cache quantization scheme that assigns each token a triaxial tag, calibrates per-tag sensitivity, and allocates INT2/INT4 bit-widths under a fixed memory budget. We implement TriAxialKV as an end-to-end serving system, comprising calibration, mixed-precision quantization and memory management, and custom fused Triton decode kernels. When using Qwen3-VL-32B-Thinking as a computer-use agent operating the OSWorld, TriAxialKV matches the accuracy of SGLang with BF16 KV cache while supporting 4.5$\times$ KV cache capacity and achieving 30% higher end-to-end throughput, when running on real GPU systems.

Machine Learning.title: Two Principles for Autoregressive Language Modeling
Machine Learning.summary: We investigate the functional differentiation learned by RoPE Transformers to derive principles for autoregressive language modeling. We introduce two intervention-based metrics: RoPE Frequency Importance Score (RFIS) measures how removing a frequency contribution changes a head's full attention distribution, and RoPE Positional Dependence (RPD) isolates the effect of rotary modulation. In Qwen3 and Llama3.1, these metrics distinguish retrieval from positional modeling, while individual heads can exhibit both functions. A mid-low-frequency Global Positional Band (GPBand) separates their frequency dependencies and tracks the training sequence length in controlled experiments, suggesting that global positional fitting can hinder zero-shot length extrapolation. These findings motivate two principles. (1) Functional Organization: retrieval and positional functions should be assigned separately and mixed within layers with layer-specific allocation; and (2) Positional Dependence: positional modeling should operate only locally, while global access should rely on position-independent retrieval. Matched pretraining from scratch and targeted architectural ablations at 380M and 1.4B parameters support both principles and highlight the importance of mechanism choice in realizing each function. Together, these findings suggest a promising route toward architectural innovation grounded in the functional requirements of autoregressive language modeling.

Machine Learning.title: From Benchmarks to the Bench: Preference, Correspondence and Selectivity in Bidirectional Drug-Target Screening
Machine Learning.summary: Identifying active molecules for known targets and potential targets for existing drugs is central to drug discovery and repurposing. Drug-target interaction (DTI) models can rank vast numbers of drug-target pairs, but limited experimental capacity restricts testing to a small number of candidates. We compared the bidirectional recommendations of 13 released systems across 711 molecular structures of FDA-approved drugs and 614 human proteins. For the same target or drug, pairs of models produced completely disjoint Top-10 molecule and protein lists in 77.8% and 70.1% of comparisons, respectively. Even where recommendations overlapped, agreement between some systems largely reflected recurring preferences for the same candidates. Published inhibition measurements for 79 molecules and 65 kinases revealed that some systems enriched active candidates, yet their hit yields changed little when recommendations were matched to different drugs or targets, whereas other systems lost substantially more hits. Some of the former systems also rarely ranked both molecules and kinases correctly when two drugs favoured different kinases. We further retrained the same architecture on the same data, with the training objective fixed and random seeds varied.
